name: Let Your Imagination Flow!🎨 Flow Matching and Rectified Flows
description:
Welcome to the Madrid ML Meetup! 🤗

LLMs with agentic loops are all the rage right now, but another family of methods plays an important role in image generation: flow models. These models learn a process that transforms samples from a simple random distribution into samples from a complex, unknown distribution represented by a large dataset. This enables the generation of synthetic data, **including images, videos, and tabular data**, in a way that scales effectively to large training datasets. 🧠

🎨 In this talk, we will provide an intuitive introduction to two popular flow methods: **Flow Matching and Rectified Flows**. Starting with simple distributions, we will explore their basic concepts before demonstrating an application using a simple image dataset. For those who want to go the extra mile, a public implementation is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/albarji/toy-flow-matching). 💻

🎤 Our speaker, **Álvaro Barbero**, holds a PhD in machine learning from the Universidad Autónoma de Madrid. His research interests include open-source large language models and image generation methods. He lectures on the master’s programme in Data Science and AI at Afi Global Education and previously served as Director of AI at the Instituto de Ingeniería del Conocimiento. He currently leads the AI Lab at Lynx Tech, a Spanish scale-up that uses the latest artificial intelligence techniques to combat fraud and money laundering in the banking sector. 🛡️

The event is organized by **Machine Learning Circle**, **Universidad Politécnica de Madrid**, **Universidad Rey Juan Carlos**, and **ARQUIMEA Research Center**, in collaboration with the **Madrid City Council**. 🏦

name: Consultas en milisegundos sobre tu data lake (sin copiar los datos)
description:
⚠️ 🇪🇸 Esta sesión será en español / This session will be in Spanish

Cada vez más empresas guardan sus datos en un data lake: en vez de meterlos en una base de datos, dejan ficheros Parquet en S3 en formato Iceberg, que se encarga de decir qué ficheros forman la tabla en cada momento. Es barato, es abierto y lo lee cualquiera. Pero no es rápido: una consulta puede tardar segundos o minutos, y la respuesta habitual de la industria sigue siendo «cópialos a otro sitio».

En esta charla veremos que no hace falta. Apache Pinot (OLAP en Java, milisegundos, miles de consultas por segundo) usa internamente un formato similar a Iceberg: ficheros inmutables y un manifiesto que decide cuáles se… leen. Como su capa de almacenamiento es una API de plugins, podemos dejar los datos donde están y guardar solo los índices al lado: más de 500 consultas por segundo por debajo del segundo sobre 12.000 millones de filas, sin duplicar un byte. Hablaremos de cómo funciona todo esto y de las situaciones donde merece la pena y, también, en las que no lo hace.

name: Grafana & Friends 🤝 Madrid GO UG
description:
The Grafana & Friends Madrid meetup is back, and this time we are partnering with the [Madrid GO User Group](https://www.meetup.com/go-mad/) and visiting our good friends at [Celonis](https://www.celonis.com/).

⚠️ For this event, RSVP at https://www.meetup.com/go-mad/events/316570374 ⚠️

🎙️ "**From Counter.Inc() to a billion series**", [Antonio Pitasi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pitasi/), Senior Software Engineer at [Grafana Labs](https://grafana.com/).

Add a counter. Two lines and you can finally see how often your service fails.
Then you add a label to tell failure reasons apart, and the counter becomes genuinely useful. You can now see why it's failing.
So you start adding more labels, one for the kind of user, one for the value of the operation. Each one seems reasonable and enables rich queries and alerts.
This talk follows that counter all the way down: from instrumenting a Go service, to how Prometheus scrapes and stores your data, to building a horizontally scalable distributed metrics database as you go from one counter to billions.

You don't need to know anything about observability to attend this session!

📍**Location:**

name: APIs for the Modern PM
description:
**Introduction**

APIs are not just an engineering concern.

They shape the customer experience, determine how products connect with third parties, and create opportunities for new functionality, data sharing and monetisation.

Join ProductTank Madrid for a practical session designed for product managers and builders who want to work more confidently with APIs.

We will explore their foundations through real-world examples, use monitoring and observability to understand journeys spanning multiple services, and examine open-data use cases across banking and transport, third-party integrations, and how greater transparency into system behaviour can create value across B2B and B2C products.

We will also look at how APIs underpin MCPs, which are driving a major shift in how people and AI agents access tools, context and services, before finishing with Q&A and networking.

**Timings**

7:00 - Welcome
7:10 - Talks begin
8:00 - Q&A
8:20 - Networking

**Speakers**

**Marisa Martin Serrano**
*Engineering Manager / Solutions Architect at EcoVadis*

Marisa is an engineering leader, solutions architect and technical product professional with 20 years of international experience across transport, finance, telecoms, consulting and other complex industries. She specialises in turning business needs into scalable technical architectures and aligning engineering delivery with product goals. She is also a public speaker and mentor with Step4ward and Tech SHEssions Madrid.
**[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/marisa-martin-serrano/)**

**Paloma Menéndez Palau**
*Head of Product at Depay*

Paloma is Head of Product at Depay and a computer science graduate specialising in scalable payment infrastructure. Her experience spans product strategy, REST API integrations, checkout and payment processing, and merchant onboarding at Depay, Yuno, AstroPay and Rappi. She works closely with engineering and commercial teams to improve reliability, reduce checkout friction and use data to increase merchant performance.
**[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/paloma-men%C3%A9ndez-palau-5b4246109/)**

**Who is this event for?**

* Product managers who want real technical fluency, not a glossary
* PMs working on platforms, integrations, payments or anything API-first
* Designers and engineers curious about how product decisions shape technical contracts
* Founders whose product is consumed by other developers
* Anyone who has ever nodded along in an architecture review and then quietly googled it afterwards

You do not need to be technical to get value from this evening. You need to be curious.

**About our sponsor — Cabify**

Huge thanks to **Cabify** for hosting us and supporting Madrid's product community.

Founded in Madrid in 2011, Cabify is an Iberoamerican multi-mobility platform connecting passengers, drivers and companies through technology.

It operates in more than 40 cities across six countries — Spain, Chile, Argentina, Peru, Colombia and Uruguay — serving over 50 million registered users and 40,000 companies, with around 1,000 employees across its offices in Spain and Latin America.

Cabify's stated ambition is to transform cities into better living spaces through mobility, built on a sustainable business model and a commitment to the UN Global Compact and the Sustainable Development Goals.
Cabify will kindly be providing drinks during the networking session.

**Networking & Q&A**

After the talks we'll open the floor for questions and debate, then stay on for drinks and conversation with Madrid's product community. ProductTank Madrid has sold out edition after edition this past year — come early, meet people, and stick around.

**Join the event**

Please only RSVP if you intend to come — and if your plans change, update your RSVP so someone else can take your spot.

name: Visita guiada a “Revolución Cuántica”
description:
¡Hola a todos, comunidad de Quantum Madrid! 👋

Esta vez cambiamos las charlas y los auditorios por una experiencia un poco diferente: nos vamos de visita a **Revolución Cuántica**, la exposición de Espacio Fundación Telefónica dedicada a explorar los fundamentos de la física cuántica y las tecnologías que están surgiendo a partir de ella. ⚛️

**🔬 La visita:**
Desde Quantum Madrid hemos organizado una **visita guiada exclusiva para la comunidad** a la exposición *Revolución Cuántica*.

La muestra propone un recorrido desde los orígenes de la mecánica cuántica hasta la actual segunda revolución cuántica, pasando por conceptos como la superposición, el entrelazamiento o el principio de incertidumbre, y por sus aplicaciones en ámbitos como la computación, las comunicaciones y la sensórica cuántica.

A través de **más de 120 piezas**, entre objetos científicos históricos, instalaciones inmersivas, audiovisuales e interactivos, podremos conocer de una forma accesible cómo la física cuántica ha cambiado nuestra comprensión del mundo y por qué está llamada a tener un impacto cada vez mayor en la tecnología y la sociedad.

Además de disfrutar de la exposición, será una buena oportunidad para reencontrarnos, conocer a otros miembros de la comunidad y seguir hablando de cuántica fuera del formato habitual de nuestras charlas.

**🗓️ Agenda (aprox.):**

* 17:15 h – Encuentro del grupo en Espacio Fundación Telefónica.
* 17:30 h – Inicio de la visita guiada a *Revolución Cuántica*.
* 18:30/18:45 h – Fin aproximado de la visita.
* Después de la visita, quienes quieran podrán quedarse a tomar algo por la zona y seguir haciendo comunidad 🍻.
* 📅 **Cuándo:** Jueves 8 de octubre de 2026 a las 17:30 h
* 📍 **Dónde:** Espacio Fundación Telefónica – C/ Fuencarral, 3, Madrid. La exposición se encuentra en la 3.ª planta.

⚠️ **IMPORTANTE: PLAZAS MUY LIMITADAS**
La visita se realizará en un grupo reducido, por lo que os pedimos que **solo os apuntéis si tenéis previsto asistir**. Si finalmente no podéis venir, por favor liberad vuestra plaza cuanto antes para que pueda aprovecharla otra persona de la comunidad.
Evento presencial y gratuito, con inscripción previa obligatoria.
